summary: Maximum input+output tokens an LLM can process in a single request, with critical performance and cost implications

content.overview: Context window (or context limit) is the maximum number of tokens (input + output combined) an LLM can process in a single request. As of 2025, leading models offer 128K-200K tokens (Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 200K, GPT-4: 128K) with some reaching 1M+ (Gemini 1.5 Pro). However, a large window doesn't mean usable capacity - performance degrades significantly as you approach limits due to 'lost-in-the-middle' effect and quadratic computational costs. Critical rule: Stay at 80-85% of max limit for reliable performance.
keyPoints: Context window includes BOTH input (prompt, conversation history, tool results) AND output (generated response) - not separate budgets
CRITICAL: 'Lost-in-the-middle' effect - LLMs heavily weight beginning and end of context, undervalue middle content (primacy/recency bias)
Computational cost scales quadratically (O(n²)) with context length - 100K tokens costs ~4x more than 50K tokens to process
Practical usability: Aim for 80-85% of theoretical max - 200K window → use max 160-170K tokens for reliable quality
Token counting is model-specific - use provider's tokenization library (tiktoken for OpenAI, Anthropic tokenizer for Claude) for accuracy
2025 standards: 128K+ is common for frontier models, 1M+ windows exist but are expensive and slower
Context overflow causes: Long conversations, large tool outputs (RAG chunks, API responses), extensive system prompts/examples

examples.title: Context Budget Breakdown
examples.code:
// 200K token context window example:
System prompt: 5K tokens
Conversation history: 80K tokens
RAG retrieved chunks: 40K tokens
Current user query: 1K tokens
TOTAL INPUT: 126K tokens

Available for output: 200K - 126K = 74K tokens
// Well within 80% limit (160K), safe to proceed
examples.explanation: Always budget context across all inputs - system prompts, history, tool results, and reserve space for output

examples.title: Lost-in-the-Middle Problem
examples.explanation: Place critical instructions at start/end of prompt, not middle - LLMs attend more to boundaries

warnings: NEVER assume full context window is usable - quality degrades significantly above 80-85% capacity
Token estimation without proper tokenizer is unreliable - 'tokens ≈ chars/4' is rough approximation, can be off by 20-30%
Exceeding context limit causes request failures or silent truncation (depending on provider) - both are bad
Large contexts increase latency exponentially - 200K token request may take 10-30+ seconds vs. 2-3 seconds for 10K tokens
Conversation history accumulates quickly - 50 turn conversation with 1K tokens/turn = 50K tokens before you add anything else
Tool outputs can explode context - single RAG retrieval might return 20-50K tokens, multiple tools compound the issue
bestPractices: Implement context management strategies BEFORE hitting limits: (1) Summarization (compress history), (2) Truncation (drop old messages), (3) Sliding window (keep recent + summary)
Use structured formatting (Markdown headers, XML tags) to help LLMs parse long contexts efficiently
Be selective with context - don't paste entire files, extract only relevant functions/sections
Monitor token usage in production - track average/peak context usage, set alerts at 70% capacity
For RAG: Limit retrieved chunks (e.g., top 5-10), rerank for relevance, truncate low-quality results
Implement periodic summarization for long conversations - compress every N turns to maintain working context
Consider model selection based on context needs - don't pay for 200K window if you only use 20K
